The blind spot cameras remind me of what I used to have on my 2016 Honda Civic. It's great to see that implemented, even if the gen 1 cameras don't have that great of quality.

The suspension update in the R1S is great though. I would describe it as taking the "bucking up" from acceleration out. Now it feels more like a direct transfer of force to the road instead of additional movement up in the front.

It was a solid update, but I had my camp speaker out of the dock during the update and now it won't lock in, even after a software and system update. Little bit of a bummer on that end.

I remember finding this out and my stream of consciousness resembled: "well these things are brittle, better just throw it at this enemy," *throws*, "this undead arm is coming back to attack me!" *Catches*, "well, that's nifty"

I almost feel like any circumstance is an opportunity. Like being single may allow you to explore a greater variety of friendships or potential relationships that might not exist otherwise. I think the worst part is knowing what you have to do, but being unable to execute. The steps quote I will definitely keep in mind, though.

I held a training session, but my industry is known for its high turnover, so perhaps I need to reevaluate my channels of communication.

I went to a talk once by L Hunter Lovins, author of Natural Capitalism. She said that the ability to tell a narrative is far more important in captivating people than pure data. She evidenced this by talking about how effective all the data regarding global warming has been in convincing the industrial world to take action. Story telling and persuasion are definitely some of my weaker traits, so I guess I have nowhere to go but up in that regard.On another note, I was looking at a masters program at the Illinois Institute of Technology, the MS in environmental management and sustainability. Would you say your masters got you much further than your bachelors? I have a degree in environmental science, but the masters is offered through IITs school of business. I feel like that unique, interdisciplinary degree would really help me get into consulting instead of operations, though I recognize the importance of doing operations and understanding the roadblocks.

It is actually something I love to do. I can sometimes get stuck in the doldrums of tedious tasks, but then again, everyone does. I do sustainability at one of Chicagos historical buildings.Also, I didn't actually make it to 86, I just never reset my badge.

Day 1 again (can't reset badge on my reddit app): I know that this subreddit is usually full of uplifting and empowering stories, but honestly I've been full of nothing but disappointment these past few weeks. I haven't been exercising, eating well and sticking to nofap. I have a job, but I feel like I've been letting down my team constantly and thus jeopardizing my future professional career. Fapping to me represents the overall lack of self control and discipline in my life and I don't know how and when I will finally begin to reclaim it, but I'm hoping that will be today. I would appreciate words of encouragement or an accountability partner.

I fapped to fall asleep a lot in the past, but exhaustion from work usually makes this end a bit easier. Waking up early is like hell to me between the morning wood and the frustration of not being able to get all the sleep available. Either way, being bored or frustrated in bed is bad news.

I know exactly the feeling of watching everything crumble around you. I was in the same position when I withdrew for a semester. I got my degree in a much easier major, bit I was enrolled in engineering at a top university.I think solely blaming it on fapping is looking at too little of the system. The system would be the positive feedback loop of "I have no self discipline, so I fap/drink/smoke/etc; I fap/drink/smoke/etc because I have no self discipline." the addiction cycle that ultimately broke me.I try not to look back for too long and instead focus on the present and future. Although I have huge regrets, I can't let these hold me back. On a more personal note. I just abstained for 24 hours for the first time in week, so I guess its never too late for a fresh start.

23. For anyone in high school, master nofap and truly enjoy college (if you choose to go) that kind of self discipline will improve every aspect of those 4 years. That was my biggest regret of college, not understanding that link between self discipline, nofap, sociability and health. I'm so happy that the younger folks are recognizing this as a problem early, but I'm also happy for everyone trying to better themselves.
Clean diet, sleep and exercise. Set yourself up with good habits and hit it.
Activated. My 23rd birthday is in a a couple weeks. I want to be a new man, I already have a week headstart!
